assumptions: The receiver and every operand have the same actual checked fixed-integer width and signedness; values remain exact BigInt.
Checked operations return the registered immutable standard Option<T>, with None for mathematical overflow or unsigned underflow.
Saturating operations clamp the mathematical result to the source type range, independent of debug or release overflow settings.
Ord min/max/clamp use the built-in implementation for primitive integers only; no arbitrary ADT trait implementation is inferred.
Reversed clamp bounds preserve a source panic as an exception, rather than a fabricated successful value or Option.
The pinned Rust 1.89 arithmetic methods are const-eligible; ordinary Ord methods are not const-eligible.
usize/isize use the existing 64-bit portable profile; other pointer profiles, mixed signed operands, floats and unbound generics require separate contracts.
No Rust execution or whole-program Router parity is established by these source-derived contracts.

Saturating operations clamp the mathematical result to the source type range, independent of debug or release overflow settings.

usize/isize use the existing 64-bit portable profile; other pointer profiles, mixed signed operands, floats and unbound generics require separate contracts.

assumptions: The receiver and every operand have the same actual checked fixed-integer width and signedness; values remain exact BigInt.
Checked operations return the registered immutable standard Option<T>, with None for mathematical overflow or unsigned underflow.
Saturating operations clamp the mathematical result to the source type range, independent of debug or release overflow settings.
Ord min/max/clamp use the built-in implementation for primitive integers only; no arbitrary ADT trait implementation is inferred.
Reversed clamp bounds preserve a source panic as an exception, rather than a fabricated successful value or Option.
The pinned Rust 1.89 arithmetic methods are const-eligible; ordinary Ord methods are not const-eligible.
usize/isize use the existing 64-bit portable profile; other pointer profiles, mixed signed operands, floats and unbound generics require separate contracts.
No Rust execution or whole-program Router parity is established by these source-derived contracts.

Shared receiver syntax and pointee identity remain checked; scalar field reads require Copy evidence, and ownership, mutation, consuming receivers, trait dispatch and unsafe operations retain their own frontend obligations.

assumptions: The receiver and every operand have the same actual checked fixed-integer width and signedness; values remain exact BigInt.
Checked operations return the registered immutable standard Option<T>, with None for mathematical overflow or unsigned underflow.
Saturating operations clamp the mathematical result to the source type range, independent of debug or release overflow settings.
Ord min/max/clamp use the built-in implementation for primitive integers only; no arbitrary ADT trait implementation is inferred.
Reversed clamp bounds preserve a source panic as an exception, rather than a fabricated successful value or Option.
The pinned Rust 1.89 arithmetic methods are const-eligible; ordinary Ord methods are not const-eligible.
usize/isize use the existing 64-bit portable profile; other pointer profiles, mixed signed operands, floats and unbound generics require separate contracts.
No Rust execution or whole-program Router parity is established by these source-derived contracts.

assumptions: The receiver and every operand have the same actual checked fixed-integer width and signedness; values remain exact BigInt.
Checked operations return the registered immutable standard Option<T>, with None for mathematical overflow or unsigned underflow.
Saturating operations clamp the mathematical result to the source type range, independent of debug or release overflow settings.
Ord min/max/clamp use the built-in implementation for primitive integers only; no arbitrary ADT trait implementation is inferred.
Reversed clamp bounds preserve a source panic as an exception, rather than a fabricated successful value or Option.
The pinned Rust 1.89 arithmetic methods are const-eligible; ordinary Ord methods are not const-eligible.
usize/isize use the existing 64-bit portable profile; other pointer profiles, mixed signed operands, floats and unbound generics require separate contracts.
No Rust execution or whole-program Router parity is established by these source-derived contracts.

assumptions: The receiver and every operand have the same actual checked fixed-integer width and signedness; values remain exact BigInt.
Checked operations return the registered immutable standard Option<T>, with None for mathematical overflow or unsigned underflow.
Saturating operations clamp the mathematical result to the source type range, independent of debug or release overflow settings.
Ord min/max/clamp use the built-in implementation for primitive integers only; no arbitrary ADT trait implementation is inferred.
Reversed clamp bounds preserve a source panic as an exception, rather than a fabricated successful value or Option.
The pinned Rust 1.89 arithmetic methods are const-eligible; ordinary Ord methods are not const-eligible.
usize/isize use the existing 64-bit portable profile; other pointer profiles, mixed signed operands, floats and unbound generics require separate contracts.
No Rust execution or whole-program Router parity is established by these source-derived contracts.

Shared receiver syntax and pointee identity remain checked; scalar field reads require Copy evidence, and ownership, mutation, consuming receivers, trait dispatch and unsafe operations retain their own frontend obligations.

assumptions: The receiver and every operand have the same actual checked fixed-integer width and signedness; values remain exact BigInt.
Checked operations return the registered immutable standard Option<T>, with None for mathematical overflow or unsigned underflow.
Saturating operations clamp the mathematical result to the source type range, independent of debug or release overflow settings.
Ord min/max/clamp use the built-in implementation for primitive integers only; no arbitrary ADT trait implementation is inferred.
Reversed clamp bounds preserve a source panic as an exception, rather than a fabricated successful value or Option.
The pinned Rust 1.89 arithmetic methods are const-eligible; ordinary Ord methods are not const-eligible.
usize/isize use the existing 64-bit portable profile; other pointer profiles, mixed signed operands, floats and unbound generics require separate contracts.
No Rust execution or whole-program Router parity is established by these source-derived contracts.

assumptions: The actual checked fixed-integer target, signedness and width determine this monomorphic parser and Result layout.
Decimal FromStr accepts an optional ASCII plus sign, and signed targets also accept minus; no whitespace trimming or JavaScript numeric coercion is introduced.
Invalid digits are checked before reporting multiplication overflow at that byte; a preceding digit overflow stops before any later invalid byte.
Machine integers remain BigInt; usize/isize aliases use the existing checked 64-bit portable profile.
FromStr and str.parse are not const-eligible; stable from_str_radix is const-eligible since Rust 1.82, with invalid radix preserving source panic behavior.
NonZero types, binary32/binary64 FromStr, generic unbound parse targets and unchecked mutation require separate contracts.
No Rust execution or complete Router parity is established by these source-derived adapters.
